payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery whose dopant suppresses negative-electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The cell achieved 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. Projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
